messages.subject: DMRs analysis
parts:
Dear All,

I am a newbie to WGBS data analysis, using methylKit for my data analysis. I have some basic questions about analyzing DMRs using methylKit.
   1) Is tiling window analysis is synonym for DMR analysis? if not can I call DMRs using methylKit.
   2) why to call tiles and what is the optimum size of a tile for better explaining differential methylation?
   3) possible downstream analysis and interpretations using tiling window analysis.

Thanks in advance. Have a good day.

Best regards
Prasad

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] DMRs analysis
parts:
On Fri, Mar 9, 2018 at 7:23 AM, Prasad Gandham <prasad...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear All,

I am a newbie to WGBS data analysis, using methylKit for my data analysis. I have some basic questions about analyzing DMRs using methylKit.
   1) Is tiling window analysis is synonym for DMR analysis? if not can I call DMRs using methylKit.
You can use eDMR package or methSeg() function from methylKit on DMCs to get DMRs that are variable length.
2) why to call tiles and what is the optimum size of a tile for better explaining differential methylation?

There is no optimum size afaik. It is mostly a strategy to deal with sparse data where you don't have coverage on exactly the same CpGs. The assumption is that CpGs nearby each other behave similarly therefore you don't need to have coverage on the same CpGs. This could also be a strategy to minimizing number of tests for whole-genome data sets.
3) possible downstream analysis and interpretations using tiling window analysis.
downstream analysis is annotating them with various genomic annotations and associating DMRs to genes.

Thanks in advance. Have a good day.

Best regards
Prasad
